Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: The records office maintains filing standards for intake documents, assigns unique identifiers to each submission, and logs custodial transfers. Standard practice requires chronological indexing of correspondence, retention of original drafts, and segregation of duties between document creation and final authorization.

2) What occurred: The actor submitted a facility inspection report into the general intake queue. A second document, mirroring the first with a corrected compliance status, was filed under a distinct identifier. The actor entered the inspector's account identifier into the payment channel's designated recipient field and initiated a transfer dated to the same period as the inspection. The original inspection report was marked as "superseded" in the status field; the altered document was moved to the primary compliance folder. The actor created a memo in the inspector's shared drive referencing "consulting services" with a date preceding the inspection.

3) Materials/access observed: One original inspection report, one altered inspection report, one payment transaction record, one internal memo document, two account identifiers, one shared drive location, and three distinct filing dates. The actor held administrative write access to the compliance folder and the inspector's shared drive during the relevant period.

4) Indicators & artifacts: The two inspection reports share identical structural fields but differ only in the "compliance status" field value. The payment transaction recipient field matches the inspector's personal account identifier rather than an institutional account. The memo's creation timestamp precedes the inspection date by 14 days. The "superseded" status field on the original report was edited after the altered document was filed, with no corresponding version-control log entry.
